description: Spectral Band Replication (SBR) decomposed. SBR is the bandwidth-extension tool used in HE-AAC and similar codecs. The encoder drops high-frequency content from the bitstream (saving substantial bits) and sends only a few side parameters; the decoder regenerates the high-frequency content by replicating lower-frequency content shifted up, then tuning it via the side parameters. Achieves perceptual-quality bandwidth doubling at near-zero additional bit cost.

sub_mechanisms.name: qmf_filterbank
sub_mechanisms.definition: SBR uses a 64-band QMF (Quadrature Mirror Filter) bank for analysis. Maps the time signal into a time-frequency grid suitable for parametric high-frequency manipulation.
sub_mechanisms.why: Different filterbank than MDCT (used by the underlying AAC core). QMF gives separate time/frequency resolution that's better suited for the patching operations SBR performs. Both filterbanks exist in HE-AAC, working in tandem.

sub_mechanisms.name: patching_high_from_low
sub_mechanisms.definition: Decoder copies QMF subbands from the low-frequency core to higher-frequency positions. E.g., subbands 8-15 get copied to slots 16-23, 24-31, etc.
sub_mechanisms.why: Music has harmonic structure — high frequencies often resemble shifted low frequencies. The patched copy is a reasonable first approximation that side parameters then refine. No explicit synthesis from scratch; just shifted copies.

sub_mechanisms.name: envelope_adjustment
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-band gain factors applied to the patched samples to match the source's high-frequency envelope.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without adjustment, the patched copy has the same energy as the original low frequencies — usually too much. Envelope gains scale each band to match the source's actual high-frequency content. Sent as small (~4-8 bits per band) side parameters.

sub_mechanisms.name: noise_addition
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-band noise level: when the source's high-frequency content is more noisy than the patched (tonal) copy can represent, add band-shaped noise.
sub_mechanisms.why: Cymbals, hi-hats, breath sounds have noise-dominated high frequencies that pure patching can't reproduce. Sending a noise-level parameter lets the decoder add synthetic noise of the right amount and band-shape. Captures the noisy texture cheaply.

sub_mechanisms.name: missing_harmonic_addition
sub_mechanisms.definition: When patching produces extra harmonics from the wrong source, encoder can signal 'missing harmonic' positions for the decoder to insert sinusoidal tones.
sub_mechanisms.why: Patching is approximation; sometimes specific harmonic content is missing or wrong. Per-block missing-harmonic positions let the encoder explicitly correct for these cases.

sub_mechanisms.name: tone_to_noise_ratio_control
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-band parameter controlling the balance between patched (tonal) and synthetic noise contributions.
sub_mechanisms.why: Different content needs different tonal/noise balance. Voiced vocals are tonal; sibilants are noisy. Per-band T/N ratio captures this. The decoder mixes patched signal + noise according to this ratio.

sub_mechanisms.name: envelope_time_resolution
sub_mechanisms.definition: SBR's envelope grid can have different time resolutions: fine grids for transients, coarse for steady-state. Signalled per frame.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same insight as window switching: transients need fine time resolution; steady-state benefits from coarse (fewer envelope updates, fewer bits). Per-frame grid adaptation matches the SBR overhead to the signal's needs.

sub_mechanisms.name: frequency_grid_alignment
sub_mechanisms.definition: The frequency grid for envelope and noise parameters aligns approximately with critical bands at high frequencies (where SBR operates).
sub_mechanisms.why: Perception of high-frequency content is critical-band based. SBR's grid matches this perceptual structure so each parameter controls roughly one critical band's worth of content.

sub_mechanisms.name: sbr_signaling_in_bitstream
sub_mechanisms.definition: SBR data carried in extension elements within the AAC bitstream. AAC-LC decoders without SBR support skip these elements; HE-AAC decoders process them.
sub_mechanisms.why: Backward compatibility: an HE-AAC stream decodes (with reduced quality) on plain AAC-LC decoders. The SBR extension is optional. Same architecture as HDR SEI in video — extensions ignorable by older decoders.

sub_mechanisms.name: downsampled_core
sub_mechanisms.definition: Often used with a downsampled AAC core (half-rate). The core codes the low frequencies at the lower rate; SBR upsamples + regenerates highs to give full rate.
sub_mechanisms.why: Saves bits on the core (lower rate = fewer samples to code). SBR fills in the high frequencies from the side info. Net effect: full-rate playback from half-rate-equivalent core bits + small SBR side info.

sub_mechanisms.name: sbr_bitrate_overhead
sub_mechanisms.definition: SBR side info is typically ~1-3 kbps regardless of stream bitrate. The core can drop ~50% of its content; net bitrate reduction is ~30-50%.
sub_mechanisms.why: SBR's side info is essentially fixed cost. At high bitrates, dropping the highs saves a lot. At low bitrates, the saved bits dramatically help quality elsewhere. The technology's sweet spot is the 32-64 kbps stereo range.

derivation_rules.name: patching_exploits_harmonic_structure
if: source high frequencies resemble shifted low frequencies
then: patching produces a reasonable approximation at zero high-band coding cost
derivation_rules.why: Musical instruments produce harmonics at integer multiples of fundamentals; harmonics are shifted versions of each other. Patching from low to high captures this naturally. Side parameters refine where the assumption breaks.

derivation_rules.name: side_parameters_replace_full_coding
if: high-frequency content can be regenerated parametrically
then: a few hundred bits per second replace tens of kilobits of coding
derivation_rules.why: Coding high frequencies as MDCT coefficients costs ~50% of the total bitrate. Sending envelope + noise + missing harmonic parameters costs ~1-3 kbps. The asymmetry is the SBR efficiency win.

derivation_rules.name: perceptual_quality_preserved_at_low_bitrates
then: SBR-based codecs (HE-AAC) outperform pure waveform codecs
derivation_rules.why: Below ~48 kbps stereo, AAC-LC's pure-waveform approach forces aggressive quantisation that audibly degrades highs. SBR sidesteps this by synthesising the highs from parameters. Quality is dramatically better at the same bitrate.

derivation_rules.name: backward_compatible_extension
if: SBR data is in optional extension elements
then: AAC-LC decoders decode the core, ignoring SBR
derivation_rules.why: Streaming and broadcast need backward compatibility with deployed AAC-LC decoders. SBR extensions are skip-safe. Older devices get worse quality (no high frequencies); newer devices get full HE-AAC. Same architecture as HDR over H.264/H.265.
